Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard `hyprland-git` package. The narrow safety gate only needs to verify that fetching sources and sourcing the PKGBUILD (including `pkgver()`) does not execute malicious code.

**Top-level scope**: Only assigns variables and declares standard packaging arrays (`depends`, `makedepends`, `optdepends`, `source`, `sha256sums`, etc.). No command substitution, no `eval`, no network calls, no obfuscation.

**Source array**: `git+https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland.git` — this is the project's own upstream repository, which is the expected source. The `SKIP` checksum is the required/standard practice for git VCS sources.

**`pkgver()` function**: Runs `git tag -l`, `git describe`, `git rev-list`, and `git rev-parse` against the already-cloned local repository to compute the version string. No network fetches, no execution of external content, no file system writes outside the cloned source directory.

`prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` are not executed during `--nobuild --noprepare`, so their contents (cmake invocation, install steps) are out of scope for this gate and will be reviewed in the full audit.

No evidence of injected malicious code or supply-chain attack vectors relevant to the sourcing/fetching step.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard hyprland-git PKGBUILD; sourcing and git fetch are safe.</summary>
</security_assessment>
